newsitem.title: ZAIRE: U.N. plane flies home 240 Zairean displaced.
newsitem.headline: U.N. plane flies home 240 Zairean displaced.

text.p: A U.N. plane flew 240 Zaireans displaced by fighting back to the eastern Zairean border town of Goma on Friday in a test run for the repatriation of up to 100,000 Rwandan refugees, a U.N. spokeswoman said.
Brenda Barton of the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) said an Ilyushin-76 transport plane carried 205 adults and 35 children from the northeastern Zairean capital of Kisangani to Goma.

"The flight was a success as loading and unloading was fast and we had two hours of fuel spare. So with our three planes we estimate we should be able to do two rotations a day, bringing the number of people we can move to 1,300 a day," she said.
WFP has offered two Ilyushin-76s and a C-130 for a planned U.N. airlift of up to 100,000 Rwandan refugees from Kisangani either to eastern Zairean border towns of straight to Rwanda.
U.N. officials said this week it might take another week to organise. It would be one of the biggest ever refugee airlifts.
U.N. agencies are concentrating on feeding the refugees and caring for the sick before the airlift. A total of 108 died at two sites south of Kisangani on Wednesday from sickness and malnutrition.
The Hutu Rwandan refugees and Zaireans were uprooted by a Tutsi-dominated rebellion in east Zaire since October and have spent much of the past six months trekking through the jungle.

Some of the refugees took part in the genocide of 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates in Rwanda in 1994. Former Rwandan troops and militiamen among them fought alongside Zairean troops against the advancing rebels in eastern Zaire.
